acceptance_signals: Doctor reports a deterministic bounded failure when Git cannot resolve the target as an accessible worktree for the current operating-system identity.
The failure message does not include raw Git stderr, an absolute host path, or host identity.
Doctor remains read-only and does not add or modify Git safe.directory configuration.
Accessible Git worktrees retain a passing repository context result and existing doctor JSON and text contracts remain valid.
Governance MCP remains required and fail-closed with unchanged protocol behavior.
Focused doctor and Codex hook tests plus the complete repository test suite pass.
Current user documentation, status, and dated evidence distinguish the controllable preflight from the unavailable Codex startup-error forwarding.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-92a6100e77834ab9ac4aa995ad804272 and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Extend the read-only AgentGov doctor journey with a deterministic bounded check that verifies the current operating-system identity can resolve the selected Git worktree before Codex starts the required Governance MCP server, while preserving existing doctor output contracts, Git ownership enforcement, and required MCP fail-closed behavior.

items: Executing Git during doctor could change performance or platform behavior, so the check must be bounded and covered on success and failure.
Reusing a hook-specific exception or message too broadly could misclassify unrelated Git errors.
Raw Git stderr may contain paths or identity details and must never enter doctor text or JSON output.
A preflight must not be presented as automatic Codex UI error forwarding.
Refactoring the shared resolver could regress existing Codex hook and MCP repository-binding behavior.
Reviewed assumption: The existing Git worktree resolution behavior can be reused or minimally extracted without changing Codex hook semantics.
Reviewed assumption: The doctor finding contract can represent the new deterministic access failure without a schema version change.
Reviewed assumption: A preflight diagnostic is the only AgentGov-controlled user-visible path established by current Codex behavior.
Reviewed assumption: The existing bounded repository-binding wording is suitable for doctor output.
Reviewed unknown: Whether the smallest implementation should expose the existing private Git resolver or inject an equivalent bounded runner into doctor tests.
Reviewed unknown: Whether README and the Governance MCP troubleshooting guide are the only user-facing documents affected after documentation tests run.

title: Detect Git worktree access failures in AgentGov doctor
